Where it began

Krishnamachari Srikkanth was born in Mylapore, Madras, on 21 December 1959. Cricket shared his time with his studies, and he qualified as an electrical engineer at the College of Engineering, Guindy.

He first played for Tamil Nadu in the 1978-79 season, and that same season he captained India in the country's first youth Test. In November 1981, aged 21, he opened with Sunil Gavaskar on his one-day debut against England at Ahmedabad, and two days later he played his first Test, at Bombay.

The player

He played 43 Tests between 1981 and 1992, scoring 2,062 runs at 29.88 with two hundreds, 12 fifties and a best of 123. His first Test hundred came at Sydney in January 1986, and the second against Pakistan at Chennai, his home ground, in 1987.

His biggest days, though, came in one-day cricket. In the 1983 World Cup final against the West Indies his 38 was the top score, and India took the trophy. In 1985 he was the leading run-scorer as India won the World Championship of Cricket, and was man of the match in the final against Pakistan. He captained India in 1989 and 1990, and it was under him that a young Sachin Tendulkar made his debut.

What made him special

He batted as if the new ball had personally offended him. Quick of eye and reflex, he pulled, hooked and drove, and lifted the ball over the infield while the fielding restrictions were on. He was pinch-hitting nearly a decade before the 1992 World Cup made it the fashion. Gavaskar, the most patient of partners, said that batting with him freed him to play his own game. Players and commentators alike counted him among the great entertainers of his day.

His bowling was less of a feature in Tests, where he never took a wicket. Yet in a one-day international against New Zealand in 1988 he made 70 and took five wickets, only the second man, after Viv Richards, to do both in the same game.

Away from the middle

He coached India A, chaired the national selectors from 2008 to 2011, a panel that chose the side that won the 2011 World Cup, and became a familiar voice in commentary. The Indian board gave him the C. K. Nayudu Lifetime Achievement Award in 2019. He has danced on Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa, been played by the actor Jiiva in the film 83, and started a YouTube channel called Cheeky Cheeka.

And finally

At Mackay in Australia, in a one-day match against Sri Lanka that was washed out after two balls, he scored a single. Until 2021 nobody else had scored a single international run there. Few batters can say they once had a whole venue's records to themselves.
